questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Exploring a new culture, while also being able to travel to new country alone and meeting new people. Furtermore, seeing how law is taught compared to here in Denmark

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say, the school and International were very helpful, but there was still some confusion in the beginning, however this could also be because I was not used to system and not the universitys fault

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The International Office, where we could contact them if we needed any help and then also orientation were we got a lot of useful information

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I would very difficult, because most places were already rented out and the places left were very expensive

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I possible start looking very early even before you know if you are going or not and then also concact the school about housing on campus or look online, where you can find registered landlords, so you do not get scammed, which we were told was a common thing because of the housing crisis in Ireland.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My place was very nice, but also one of the most expensive places in the town and from what I heard and saw, if you got are cheaper or very cheap place it was also not the best place to live at. However, this is not the fault of the school, but just the situation in generel in Ireland

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I cannot remember it completly, but I do remember that it was not to difficult

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The school helped

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was pretty succesful. Where I almost received all classes which I applied for, however because of some time clashes and because and lack of interest  in some of the classes I applied for in the beginning I ended up changing, which meant that I also received some classes which I did not want to in the beginning, but they ended being more interesting that I thought.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe having at least 10 classes which you like, so that if you would like to change classes or need to you have some backups.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I felt like, it was not that difficult following the classes, but the MA were more interesting and thought better.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I would so the main difference was the lack of preparation from us student. Where in Denmark you would need to have read every text before class and be able to join in the discussions, in Ireland that was not necessarily needed or expected in the same way

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Human Rights Law
International Environmental Law
Privacy and Data Protection Law
Business and Human Rights Law
Introduction to Conflict Resolution
Foundations of Childrens Rights

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Business and Human Rights Law, mostly because it seemed very different, but the teacher made it very interesting to follow.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My computer broke, so I had to buy a new one.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I would say if you get a bus cart the busses become extremely cheap compared to Denmark, the same which the public bikes you could around in town, for 10 euros a year you can use them as much as you wanted to. Something very expensive was cigarates which were around 18 euros.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The school had a great list of societies and club that everybody could join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would say join at least one society and/or club to meet irish people and also to become part of the culture.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on as many trips as possible, either the ones held by the school/socities or with friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Joining a club or society.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing specific

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I would say it was pretty easy to talk to the people, which was nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go on as many trips as possible, It is okay to ask for extensions for your assignments or exams because it is very common, Do not be shy in the beginning everybody is looking to meet new people, so ask you can also join the party, trip or if some people go out for a coffee, especially in the beginning.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: While we all want to have fun, try to make sure you have money for the whole trip, so you are not completly broke the last month or two.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting the people I spend my time with

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting use to the school system.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
